title: Bargello
summary: Bargello, also called Florentine work, is canvas embroidery in long upright wool stitches. Each row steps up and down in a zigzag, and shaded colours turn the rows into flames, waves and peaks. It makes sturdy cushions, chair seats and belts.
howToPlay: Pick a wool colour from the balls and a flame shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the canvas to stitch that shape there; it is mirrored across and down.
Copy the panel shown on the chart, then press Check.
rules: The panel is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you stitch is also stitched on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its wool colour both match the panel you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: The name is usually traced to a set of seventeenth-century chairs, covered in this stitch, kept in the Bargello museum in Florence. The same zigzag work is known in Hungary as Hungarian point, and it is still stitched for upholstery, cushions and belts.
